newsitem.title: USA: MGE spring wheat closes higher on weather, cash.
newsitem.headline: MGE spring wheat closes higher on weather, cash.

text.p: Harsh weather in the Dakotas which was stifling an already slow pace of farmer and reseller movement boosted MGE spring wheat futures to a higher close, led by the nearby March contract, traders said.
"Everyone is snowed in and there's not much selling anywhere. The spot (nearby cash) premiums on the floor (MGE trading floor) were going through the roof," a trader said.
The traders said mills were having difficulty originating wheat due to the blizzard in the upper Midwest.
"Because of the weather in North Dakota, farmers haven't moved much wheat," the trader said.
The March/May traded early at 22 cents per bushel premium the March, but profit taking of the spread brought the May back to within 20 cents of the March by the close.
Atwood Peavey took profits on the March/May and unwound two million bushels of that spread in late dealings, the traders said.
Deferred months sagged quietly on drops in the Chicago July which was tied to diminished concerns about winterkill in the U.S. winter wheat growing region.
MGE spring wheat closed 3/4 to 2-3/4 cents per bushel higher, with March up 2-3/4 at $3.95-1/4.
